⚖️ A Powerful Reminder: Justice Must Reach the Person Standing at the Lowest Pedestal

I recently studied the significant judgment of the Hon’ble Patna High Court in Gauri Shankar Ram v. State of Bihar & Ors., Criminal Writ Jurisdiction Case No. 1029 of 2026, decided on 7 August 2026.

The judgment, delivered by Hon’ble Mr. Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Hon’ble Mr. Justice Alok Kumar Sinha, highlights one of the most fundamental responsibilities of the justice delivery system: to ensure that truth is revealed and justice reaches even the most vulnerable person.

The Court observed that the investigation had suffered from serious delay and lack of proper direction. Considering the exceptional circumstances and the loss of confidence in the State investigating agency, the Court directed that the investigation be transferred to the CBI forthwith.

What particularly stood out to me was the Court’s powerful observation:

"If the Investigating Agency and the Court fail to ensure that the truth is revealed and the petitioner gets justice, it will be the failure of the entire justice delivery system.”

As a law student, I find this judgment deeply significant. It reminds us that access to justice is not merely about having courts and laws - it is about ensuring that every individual, irrespective of social or economic position, has a genuine opportunity to obtain justice.

This case also reinforces the importance of:
1.Fair and impartial investigation
2 Accountability of investigating agencies
3. Protection of vulnerable witnesses
4. Judicial monitoring in exceptional circumstances
5.Access to justice for weaker sections of society

Justice is meaningful only when it reaches those who need it the most.

— Sudhanshu Kumar
BBA LL.B. (Hons.) | Law Student

comment: A key challenge after transferring investigations is ensuring institutional accountability does not end with a change of agency. Timely supervision and witness protection remain critical for restoring confidence in the process.
